description: Table 2 is a single image-rendered data table — no axes, scale bars, micrographs or sub-panels — that tabulates Vickers hardness (HV) of the "15Al" Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steel after solution treatment and aging. Row labels are the six aging conditions: 525 °C aging, 550 °C aging, 575 °C aging, 600 °C aging, 625 °C aging and 650 °C aging; column labels are Solution-treated, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h and 10 h. Every cell gives a mean ± standard deviation, the value and its ± uncertainty wrapped onto separate lines. A single solution-treated entry, 253.4 ± 2.1 HV, appears once in the 600 °C row, i.e. the common as-solutionised baseline. The table's maximum is 965.6 ± 7.6 HV (600 °C, 6 h) and its minimum printed value is 379.8 ± 19.1 HV (525 °C, 1 h). At 525 and 550 °C the 1 h hardness is still low (379.8 and 380.2 HV) and jumps to 916.8 and 957.1 HV by 6 h. At 575 °C hardening is already rapid (752.6 ± 50.7 HV at 1 h, the largest scatter). At 625 and 650 °C hardness plateaus near 888 and 862 HV, and at 650 °C it decreases monotonically from 857.1 ± 15.4 (1 h) to 842.3 ± 3.7 HV (10 h). The table demonstrates that aging temperature and time jointly tune hardness over an ultrawide 253.4-965.6 HV window, optimum near 600 °C/6 h.

observations.observation: Table 2 reports Vickers hardness (HV) as mean ± standard deviation for the 15Al alloy aged for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h at 525, 550, 575, 600, 625 and 650 °C.
The maximum value in the table is 965.6 ± 7.6 HV, obtained at 600 °C aging for 6 h.
The lowest printed hardness in the table is 379.8 ± 19.1 HV at 525 °C aging for 1 h.
A single solution-treated value, 253.4 ± 2.1 HV, is printed once in the 600 °C aging row (the common solution-treated baseline for all aging rows).
At 525 °C aging hardness rises from 379.8 ± 19.1 HV (1 h) to 872.0 ± 21.2 HV (3 h), 916.8 ± 8.7 HV (6 h) and 915.7 ± 9.5 HV (10 h).
At 550 °C aging hardness rises from 380.2 ± 15.5 HV (1 h) to 790.3 ± 23.5 HV (3 h), 957.1 ± 15.5 HV (6 h) and 961.1 ± 19.6 HV (10 h).
575 °C aging already gives the highest 1 h hardness, 752.6 ± 50.7 HV, and the largest standard deviation (±50.7) of any cell.
600 °C aging reaches 904.9 ± 30.2 HV at 1 h, peaks at 965.6 ± 7.6 HV at 6 h, then falls slightly to 948.6 ± 12.8 HV at 10 h.
At 625 °C aging hardness stays nearly constant across time: 852.8 ± 24.6 (1 h), 889.9 ± 4.3 (3 h), 887.2 ± 14.1 (6 h) and 888.2 ± 6.6 HV (10 h).
At 650 °C aging hardness decreases monotonically with time, from 857.1 ± 15.4 HV (1 h) to 852.3 ± 13.8 (3 h), 862.8 ± 11.3 (6 h) and 842.3 ± 3.7 HV (10 h).
The caption states that the table gives Vickers hardness values of the 15Al alloys after different aging treatments.
The abstract states the Fe-35Mn-(15,17,19)Al-5Cu (at.%) low-density steels span an ultrawide hardness range from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV, which matches the minimum and maximum printed in this table.
